strings.d1.s0.name: Phuket Old Town Thalang Road
strings.d1.s0.tips: Colourful Sino-Portuguese shopfronts; cafes open in the morning, and on Sundays the street becomes a pedestrian market.
strings.d1.s1.name: Phuket Thai Hua Museum
strings.d1.s1.tips: The story of Chinese immigrants, in an air-conditioned former school building.
strings.d1.s2.name: One Chun Cafe Phuket
strings.d1.s2.tips: Michelin Bib Gourmand local cooking; try moo hong (braised pork belly) and crab.
strings.d1.s3.name: Big Buddha Phuket
strings.d1.s3.tips: A 45 m marble Buddha on the hilltop with 360° views of the island. Cover shoulders and knees; get there by taxi or scooter.
strings.d1.s4.name: Wat Chalong
strings.d1.s4.tips: Phuket's most important temple, known for the firecracker wish-making tradition.
strings.d1.b0.name: Kopitiam by Wilai
strings.d1.b1.name: Khao Rang Hill
strings.d1.b1.tips: A hilltop viewpoint over the city, close to Big Buddha, so a good alternative.
strings.d2.s0.name: Kata Noi Beach
strings.d2.s0.tips: Monsoon swells: don't swim when the red flag is up. Come in the morning for a walk or a surf lesson.
strings.d2.s1.name: Kata Beach Street Stalls
strings.d2.s1.tips: Pad thai and mango sticky rice just behind the beach.
strings.d2.s2.name: Karon Beach
strings.d2.s2.tips: An empty beach in summer, good for a walk and watching the waves.
strings.d2.s3.name: Karon Viewpoint
strings.d2.s3.tips: A viewpoint that takes in three bays at once; go before sunset.
strings.d2.s4.name: Kata Night Market
strings.d2.s4.tips: A night market in central Kata with grilled seafood and roti.
strings.d2.b0.name: Kampong Kata Hill Restaurant
strings.d2.b0.tips: A Thai restaurant packed with antiques, in Kata.
strings.d2.b1.name: Dino Park Mini Golf
strings.d2.b1.tips: A rainy-day option for families with kids, in Karon.
strings.d3.s0.name: James Bond Island Khao Phing Kan
strings.d3.s0.tips: Canoe tour (~1,500 THB). The bay stays calm even in summer, with limestone islands and caves.
strings.d3.s1.name: Koh Panyee
strings.d3.s1.tips: A Muslim fishing village built on stilts; have lunch on the boat.
strings.d3.s2.name: Hong Island Kano
strings.d3.s2.tips: Canoe into the sea caves; included in the tour.
strings.d3.s3.name: Suwan Kuha Temple
strings.d3.s3.tips: A cave temple with monkeys and a reclining Buddha.
strings.d3.s4.name: Rawai Seafood Market
strings.d3.s4.tips: Pick your fish at the market in Rawai and have it cooked across the way. Phuket's most famous seafood evening.
strings.d3.b0.name: Kan Eang at Pier Chalong
strings.d3.b0.tips: Seafood at Chalong Pier, as an alternative to Rawai.
strings.d3.b1.name: Coral Island Koh Hae
strings.d3.b1.tips: A nearby island for a half-day trip if Phi Phi is cancelled.
strings.d4.s0.name: Freedom Beach
strings.d4.s0.tips: Boats don't run in monsoon swells; instead, walk to Tri Trang beach from Patong.
strings.d4.s1.name: Patong Beach
strings.d4.s1.tips: The island's busiest beach: good for a walk and jet skis (haggle).
strings.d4.s2.name: No.6 Restaurant Patong
strings.d4.s2.tips: A cheap Thai eatery in Patong with a fast-moving queue; try the tom yum.
strings.d4.s3.name: Jungceylon Shopping Mall
strings.d4.s3.tips: An air-conditioned mall for a break from the rain and heat.
strings.d4.s4.name: Bangla Road
strings.d4.s4.tips: Patong's nightlife street with bars and shows; watch your wallet.
strings.d4.b0.name: Baan Rim Pa Patong
strings.d4.b0.tips: Royal Thai cuisine on the cliffs, with sunset views.
strings.d4.b1.name: Simon Cabaret Phuket
strings.d4.b1.tips: A cabaret show, as an alternative to Bangla Road.
strings.d5.s0.name: Nai Harn Beach
strings.d5.s0.tips: Monsoon swells. Come in the morning for a walk and a stroll along the lake.
strings.d5.s1.name: Nai Harn Beach Stalls
strings.d5.s1.tips: Grilled food and fruit shakes behind the beach.
strings.d5.s2.name: Windmill Viewpoint
strings.d5.s2.tips: A viewpoint by the wind turbine, looking over Nai Harn and Ya Nui.
strings.d5.s3.name: Promthep Cape
strings.d5.s3.tips: The island's southernmost tip and Phuket's most famous sunset; claim a spot an hour early.
strings.d5.b0.name: Rawai Beach Restaurant
strings.d5.b0.tips: Thai food on the Rawai seafront.
strings.d5.b1.name: Ya Nui Beach
strings.d5.b1.tips: A tiny snorkelling cove below Promthep.
strings.d6.s0.name: Phuket Elephant Sanctuary
strings.d6.s0.tips: An ethical elephant sanctuary: half a day of feeding and mud baths (~3,000 THB), with no riding.
strings.d6.s1.name: Elephant Sanctuary Vegetarian Lunch
strings.d6.s1.tips: Vegetarian lunch included in the tour.
strings.d6.s2.name: Bang Pae Waterfall
strings.d6.s2.tips: A waterfall in the Khao Phra Thaeo forest, full of water in summer; a 20-minute walk.
strings.d6.b0.name: Phuket Town Lock Tien
strings.d6.b1.name: Gibbon Rehabilitation Project
strings.d6.b1.tips: Gibbon conservation, next to the waterfall.
strings.d7.theme: Old Town morning and a gentle goodbye
strings.d7.s0.name: Old Town Soi Romanee
strings.d7.s0.tips: The most photogenic street, best in the morning light.
strings.d7.s1.name: Torry's Ice Cream Phuket
strings.d7.s1.tips: Local ice cream in Old Town; try the coconut.
strings.d7.s2.name: Blue Elephant Phuket
strings.d7.s2.tips: Royal Thai cuisine in a mansion for a farewell lunch; cooking classes are also available.
strings.d7.s3.name: Phuket Airport Road Sirinat
strings.d7.s3.tips: The airport is 45 minutes away; time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Ka Jok See Phuket
strings.d7.b0.tips: Thai food in an old house.
strings.d7.b1.name: Sirinat National Park Nai Yang
strings.d7.b1.tips: A beach next to the airport, good for watching planes.
strings.note0: There is no public transport in Phuket: use a scooter (licence and helmet required), Grab or a hotel taxi. Tuk-tuks are expensive, so haggle.
strings.note1: June to October is monsoon season: don't swim when the red flag is up (currents), boat tours may be cancelled, and showers fall in the afternoon. Favour Phang Nga Bay and indoor activities.
strings.note2: Book boat tours online with hotel pickup included, and bring seasickness pills and reef-safe sunscreen.
strings.note3: Choose seafood by the kilo at Rawai market; the cooking fee is charged separately per person.
strings.note4: Cover shoulders and knees at temples; on Bangla Road, ask the price of drinks first.
strings.note5: Don't ride elephants; choose ethical sanctuaries.
